title: From Set Metrics to Ranked Metrics: Visual Guide
outline: Title: From Set Metrics to Ranked Metrics: Visual Guide

1. Cutoff Is The Threshold | a slider that cuts the ranking at k, labelling every rank TP/FP/FN/TN and recomputing P@k, R@k and F1 over System A's relevant documents at 1, 3, 5, 10 | the retriever hands you no set, so the cutoff supplies it and the rank cutoff plays exactly the role the score threshold played for a classifier

2. Blind Inside The Cutoff | a tappable 10-rank grid where the learner places four relevant documents anywhere, with presets for System A (1,3,5,10) and System B (6,7,8,9) | P@10 and R@10 are pinned at 0.40 and 1.00 however the four are arranged, so a single-cutoff metric sees membership of the top-k and never order inside it

3. Choosing k By Consumer | three consumption points (results page, RAG prompt of 5 chunks, first-stage candidate generator) plus a slider over R showing the P@10 ceiling and R-precision | the cutoff is a fact about who reads the list, and missed recall at the first stage is unfixable downstream while poor precision there is merely work for the next stage

4. Building Average Precision | the fourth relevant document dragged from rank 6 to never-retrieved, with each P@rank term, the running AP, and the uninterpolated precision-recall staircase shaded | AP sees the position of every relevant document and is the area under that curve, a Riemann sum of width 1/R, while P@10 stays frozen until the document crosses the cutoff

5. First Hit Only | four queries with draggable first-relevant ranks, per-query RR, the cost of one rank worse, and a 3-vs-4-query toggle reproducing MRR 0.583 and 0.438 | the reciprocal is top-heavy and bounded so no single disaster dominates the mean, MRR equals MAP when every query has one relevant document, and 1/MRR is never the average rank
